purpose: Independently compare an unnamed HydroLAKES Asia feature near the approximate Lake Sampaloc locality with a named OpenStreetMap relation, then screen GBIF occurrences using the named community-mapped polygon.

geometryComparison.method: Assembled the six OSM outer ways into one polygon; compared it with HydroLAKES Hylak_id 1397813 after projecting both WGS 84 geometries to UTM zone 51N (EPSG:32651).
geometryComparison.interpretation: Strong spatial correspondence supports treating Hylak_id 1397813 as the same mapped waterbody represented by the named OSM relation. OSM is community-maintained, not an authoritative survey or legal boundary; comparison does not establish positional accuracy or app suitability.

limitations: OpenStreetMap is community-contributed. Its feature name and mapped water outline are useful for a crosswalk but do not independently certify the lake boundary or positional accuracy.
OSM data is ODbL-licensed and requires attribution; distribution of an adapted database has share-alike obligations. No app geometry or adapted public database was produced.
The HydroLAKES feature is a derivative discovery polygon with a 10-hectare source threshold; other waterbody types and smaller waters are outside its complete coverage.
A zero-result GBIF query is a bounded indexed-occurrence result, not evidence that Lake Sampaloc has no fish or a complete local fish survey.
No fish species, diet, current-presence, fishing access, legal status, or app-ready boundary was established.
nextAction: If exact public-app geometry is needed, request a local authoritative map or survey crosswalk and review ODbL compatibility for the planned data distribution. Otherwise keep both polygons as research-only discovery references and continue to other CALABARZON waterbody leads.
